column2: If a poor man enjoyed the happiness of the wealthy, then the world would be; if a dog by its strength conquered a lion, then the world would be.
If the heart of the wise were known by fools, it would be imagination; if a dog drank the ocean entirely, then it would be mind.
If pure space fell among men, then the world; or if the sky fell on earth, a sky-flower would be fragrant.
If a forest grew in pure space and moved, then the world; if there were a reflection in a bare mirror, then the world.
In the womb of the unborn there is no world; in the womb of the Self there is no world; in every way, imagining of difference, duality and non-duality does not exist.
If this difference, the effect of illusion, exists, there is contemplation of Brahman; if "I am the body" is sorrow, the certainty is "I am Brahman."
When the knot of the heart exists, the wheel of Brahman cuts it; when doubt arises, one should take refuge in the certainty of Brahman.
If the thief in the form of the non-Self exists, guard the jewel of the Self; Brahman, made of eternal bliss, alone, always by itself.
By such good examples Brahman alone is established; Brahman alone is all becoming — abandon the name "world."
Having ascertained "I am Brahman," give up the sense of "I"; everything goes to dissolution like a flower in the hand of one asleep.
No body, no actions: all is Brahman alone. No element, no effect, no fourfold state.
Knowledge of the three characteristics: all is Brahman alone; abandoning all activity, contemplate "I am Brahman."
I am Brahman — no doubt; I am Brahman, the Self of consciousness; having ascertained "I am mere being-consciousness-bliss," abandon even that.
This great scripture in Shankara's line is not to be given to just anyone — not to the unbeliever, the ungrateful, the ill-behaved, the evil-minded.
It should be given to the great-souled whose inner instrument is purified by devotion to the teacher, after careful testing for a month, six months or a year.
Giving up with respect the study of all other Upanishads, one should always joyfully study the Tejobindu Upanishad.
In the boundless waters, in the midst of the world, on the back of heaven, greater than the great, entered into the lights with brilliance, Prajapati moves within the womb.
In whom all this comes together and unfolds, in whom all the gods have sat down; that alone is what has been and what will be; that is in the imperishable, in the supreme space.
By whom space, heaven and earth are covered; by whom the sun burns with radiant light; whom the seers weave within the sea; in whose imperishable supreme the creatures are.
From whom the creators of the world were born, who sent forth living beings on earth with water; who entered with the plants men and cattle and beings moving and unmoving.
Beyond this there is nothing subtler, the highest of the high, the greatest of the great; that one, unmanifest, of infinite form, the ancient universe, beyond darkness.
That they call truth and reality; that is the supreme Brahman of the seers; sacrifices and gifts, born in many ways, being born, the navel of the world bears the universe.
That is Agni, that Vayu, that the Sun, that also the Moon; that is the bright, the immortal; that is Brahman, that the waters, he is Prajapati.
All the twinklings were born of the Person like lightning; the moments, the hours, the periods, the days and nights, in all ways.
May the half-months, months, seasons and the year be ordered. He milked these two waters, and the air and heaven.
No one has grasped him above, across or in the middle. There is no ruler of him; his name is great glory.
His form does not stand in sight; no one sees him with the eye. Conceived by the heart, by the mind, by thought — those who know him become immortal.

The Paramatma-Hiranyagarbha Sukta: Hiranyagarbha arose from the waters, eight verses. Arisen from the waters, from earth and from the essence, of Vishvakarman it came about; Tvashtar, ordering its form, comes to it; that is the Person's universe in the beginning. (1) I know this great Person, sun-colored, beyond darkness; knowing him thus one becomes immortal here; there is no other path to go. (2) Prajapati moves within the womb; unborn, he is born in many ways; the wise know his source; the ordainers seek the place of the rays. (3) Who shines for the gods, who is household priest of the gods, who was born before the gods — homage to the shining Brahmin. (4) The gods, begetting the shining Brahman, said at first: "The Brahmin who knows you thus — the gods will be in his power." (5) Modesty and Lakshmi are your two wives; day and night are your sides, the stars your form, the Ashvins your open mouth; he desired, he desired this, he desired all. (6) Thus the Uttara-Narayana anuvaka. Hiranyagarbha arose in the beginning; born, he was the one lord of being; he held the earth and this heaven. To which god shall we offer with oblation?
Who by his greatness alone became king of the breathing, the winking world, who rules over this two-footed and four-footed — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
Who gives self, who gives strength, whose command all, whose command the gods obey; whose shadow is immortality, whose is death — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
Whose greatness these snowy mountains declare, whose the ocean with the Rasa they say; whose these quarters are, whose arms — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
Whom the two crying hosts, supported by his help, trembling in mind, looked upon, where the risen sun shines — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
By whom heaven is fierce and earth firm, by whom the sky is propped, by whom the vault of heaven; who is the measurer of space in the air — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
When the great waters came bearing the whole world, holding skill, begetting Agni, thence arose the one life-breath of the gods — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
Who by his greatness looked over the waters bearing skill and begetting Agni, who alone is god over the gods — to which god shall we offer with oblation?
This god is in all directions; he was born first and he is within the womb. He is being born and will be born, standing with faces turned every way.
With eyes everywhere and mouths everywhere, with hands everywhere and feet everywhere; he joins with arms and with wings, the one god begetting heaven and earth.
Vena, seeing that, knowing all worlds, where the whole universe becomes one nest; in whom all this comes together and unfolds, woven and interwoven, the all-pervading in creatures.
I declare that immortality, knowing now: the Gandharva named hidden in the caves; three steps are hidden in the caves; he who knows it is the father of Savitar, the true.
He is our kinsman, begetter, arranger; he knows all the abodes and worlds; where the gods, enjoying immortality, reached the third abodes.
They go around heaven and earth at once, around the worlds, around the directions, around the heaven; unfolding the extended thread of truth, he saw it, and it became in the creatures.
Going around the worlds, around the beings, around all the quarters and directions, Prajapati, first-born of truth, by the Self came into being as the Self.
I have sought the wondrous lord of the assembly, dear to Indra, desirable — a gift of insight.
Blaze up, Jatavedas, destroying my Nirriti; bring me cattle and life, and point out the directions.
Do not harm our cow, horse, man or world, Jatavedas; come, Agni, not bearing; do not let me fall from glory.
We know the Person; we meditate on the thousand-eyed Mahadeva; may Rudra urge us on that.
Of the Gayatri: We know the Person; we meditate on Mahadeva; may Rudra urge us on that.
We know the Person; we meditate on the curved-trunked one; may the tusked one urge us on that.
We know the Person; we meditate on the wheel-trunked one; may Nandi urge us on that.
We know the Person; we meditate on Mahasena; may the six-faced one urge us on that.
We know the Person; we meditate on the golden-winged one; may Garuda urge us on that.
We know the Self of the Veda; we meditate on Hiranyagarbha; may Brahma urge us on that.
We know Narayana; we meditate on Vasudeva; may Vishnu urge us on that.
We know the thunderbolt-nailed; we meditate on the sharp-fanged; may Narasimha urge us on that.
We know the Sun; we meditate on the maker of great light; may Aditya urge us on that.
We know Vaishvanara; we meditate on the playful one; may Agni urge us on that.
We know Katyayana; we meditate on the maiden Kumari; may Durga urge us on that.

We know the four-faced; we meditate on the bearer of the water-pot; may Brahma urge us on that. We know Aditya; we meditate on the thousand-rayed; may Bhanu urge us on that. We know the Purifier; we meditate on the seven-tongued; may Vaishvanara urge us on that. We know the great trident-bearer; we meditate on Mahadurga; may the Goddess urge us on that. We know the fortunate; we meditate on the lotus-garlanded; may Gauri urge us on that. We know the nine-clan one; we meditate on the poison-fanged; may the Serpent urge us on that. The goddess Durva, of a thousand supreme virtues, hundred-rooted, hundred-sprouted, may she remove all my sin, destroyer of bad dreams.
Sprouting from joint to joint, from knot to knot, so spread for us, O Durva, with a thousand and a hundred.
You who spread with a hundred and sprout with a thousand — to you, goddess brick, may we offer with oblation.
O Earth, stepped on by horses, stepped on by chariots, stepped on by Vishnu, I shall bear you on my head; protect me at every step.
The earth is the cow, the bearer, the sustainer of the world; you were lifted up by Varaha, the black one of a hundred arms.
Clay, destroy the sin that I have done as evil. Clay, you were given by Brahma, consecrated by Kashyapa. Clay, give me nourishment; in you all is established.
Clay, being established, drive out all that of mine, O clay; by the sin destroyed by you I go to the supreme goal.
From whatever we fear, Indra, make us safe from that; bounteous one, help us for our protection; drive away foes and enemies.
Giver of welfare, lord of the clans, Vritra-slayer, subduer of enemies, master — may bull Indra go before us, giver of welfare, maker of fearlessness.
May Indra of ancient fame bring us well-being; may Pushan, the all-knower, bring us well-being; may Tarkshya of unharmed felly bring us well-being; may Brihaspati grant us well-being.
The one of fury, the thrower of stones, the shaker, the pig-bearer, the arrow-user, the owner of the stream; Soma has conquered all the pressings; the rivals did not harm Indra.
The first born of Brahman, in the beginning, from the border, the shining Vena uncovered; he opened the depths, the nearest places, the womb of being and non-being.
Be gracious, O Earth, the dwelling and refuge of men; give us wide-spread shelter.
I invoke here that Shri, whose door is fragrance, hard to overpower, ever nourishing, rich in cattle-dung, mistress of all beings.
May Shri be mine; may Alakshmi perish. The gods led by Vishnu conquered these worlds unconquerably with the meters. May great Indra, thunderbolt-armed, the sixteenth, give shelter.
May the bounteous one bring us well-being; may he slay the sin that hates us.
Make the soma ring, O Brahmanaspati, for Kakshivan, the son of Ushij; may the body, the sacrifice-defiling debt, sit in him who hates us.
The pure ancient path stretched, by which, purified, one crosses evils; by that pure, clean path, purified, may we cross sin and the enemy.
Together with Indra, with the troop of Maruts, drink the soma, Vritra-slayer, brave and knowing; slay the foes, drive off the enemies, and make us fearless on every side.
May the waters and plants be good friends to us; may they be bad friends to him who hates us and whom we hate.

You waters are indeed bringers of comfort; place us in strength for great delight and sight. Give us here a share of your most auspicious essence, like longing mothers. We come fully to that for whose dwelling you quicken us, O waters; and you beget us.
I take refuge in golden-horned Varuna; grant me a ford when asked — whatever I have eaten of the wicked and accepted from sinners.
Whatever wrong I have done by mind, speech or deed, may Indra, Varuna, Brihaspati and Savitar purify that again and again.
Homage to Agni of the waters; homage to Indra; homage to Varuna; homage to Varuni; homage to the waters.
Whatever of the waters is cruel, unclean, unquiet, let that depart.
From overeating, over-drinking, and from fierce acceptance of gifts, may King Varuna touch that of mine with his hand.
May I, sinless, free of dust, released, free of stain, ascending the back of heaven, go to union with Brahma's world.
And Varuna who is in the waters, the sin-effacer, may he purify.
O Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Shutudri, accept this my hymn together with Parushni; Asikni with the Maruts' strengthener, Vitasta, Arjikiya, hear with Sushoma.
Truth and reality were born from kindled austerity; from that night was born; from that the ocean, the flood.
From the ocean, the flood, the year was born, ordering days and nights, the master of every winking being.
The creator fashioned Sun and Moon as before; heaven, earth, the air, and then the sun-world.

Whatever dust is on the earth, in the air, in the two worlds, may Varuna of the waters, the sin-effacer, purify these. May the Vasus purify; may Varuna purify; may the sin-effacer purify. This one is the guardian in the middle of beings, of the world. This is the world of the virtuous; this is the golden of death; the golden between heaven and earth is joined with heaven. May he instruct us in heaven.
Moist, blazing light I am. The light blazes; I am Brahman. Who I am, I am Brahman. I am, I am Brahman. I alone offer myself to myself: svaha.
The one who has done forbidden acts, the thief, the killer of an embryo, the violator of a teacher's bed — Varuna, the sin-effacer of the waters; from that sin he is freed.
Dust, earth — make me weep; the steadfast declare.
The ocean has stepped out in the first rite, begetting offspring, king of the world; the bull on the high woolen peak, great Soma, sounding drop, has grown.
We press soma for Jatavedas; he consumes the wealth of the hostile. May he carry us across all difficulties, as a boat over the river; Agni across evil.
Durga Sukta. Her, fire-colored, blazing with austerity, the daughter of Virochana, enjoyed in the fruits of action — I take refuge in the goddess Durga; homage to you who ferry well across.
Agni, new, carry us across with blessings over all difficulties; be wide for us as the fort, as the broad earth; be kind to our children and grandchildren.
O Jatavedas, destroyer of all difficulties, you carry us across evil as a boat across a river; Agni, praised with mind like Atri, awaken as protector of our bodies.
We call Agni, the conqueror of armies, the overcomer, the fierce, from the highest seat; may he carry us across all difficulties, the god Agni across evil, across the earth.
You are ancient, to be praised at sacrifices; ever the priest, and new, you sit; Agni, delight your own body and sacrifice good fortune for us.
